newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Opel Belgium metamorphosis complete August 97.
newsitem.headline: Opel Belgium metamorphosis complete August 97.

text.p: Opel Belgium, a subsidiary of U.S. car maker General Motors (GM), on Tuesday produced its 10 millionth car and said that a $533 million investment programme would be completed next August.

"We had to carry out this changing process...to safeguard the future of this company and employment, and if Opel Belgium wanted to keep its place as one of the main international GM production centres," Opel Belgium president and managing director Leo Valvekens told a news conference.
"We're ready to become the plant with the highest quality in Europe," he said.
Valvekens said Opel Belgium's expertise in modernising its plant would be applied at other GM companies in Europe, Latin America and South East Asia.
Opel Belgium, based in the port of Antwerp in northern Belgium, has a workforce of 7,800.
The plant will produce about 300,000 cars this year -- about 70 percent of them Opel Astras and the rest Vectras -- compared with 304,505 in 1995 and 319,000 in 1994.
But spokesman Dirk Snauwaert said Opel Belgium had managed to maintain production despite the works at the plant.

Opel Belgium exports 95 percent of its output to more than 50 countries. Germany is its main market, importing between 40 to 45 percent of production in Antwerp. The Netherlands is the second biggest market with about 15 percent while exports to France and southern Europe are on the rise, Snauwaert said.
Valvekens said Opel Belgium suffered from the handicap of steep social and fiscal costs in Belgium.
"Internationally we are not on the top shelf due to high government spending, taxes and... complicated laws," he said. "That's precisely why all these changes are needed."
